newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index options remain handcuffed.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index options remain handcuffed.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan spoke before the U.S. House budget committee Tuesday, but his scheduled testimony Wednesday before another committee kept index options activity in the doldrums, traders said.
"There's nothing going on," a broker in the S&P 500 index and the S&P 100 index said.
"Everyone is waiting for the Fed warrior to talk," he said, referring to Greenspan. "Hopefully that will set the tone into the number Friday.
The February U.S. employment report is scheduled for release Friday before the stock market opens.
Greenspan said Tuesday his recent comments on the stock and bond markets, which knocked both for sharp losses, were meant only to explain Fed thinking, not to move the markets.
But traders remained wary.
"If he doesn't think he's going to affect markets, then he shouldn't say anything," one SPX trader said. "It's typical political doubletalk."

The trader said that unless Greenspan makes a comment like last December's remark that the financial markets had been subject to "irrational exuberance," the market will likely stay locked in a range until Friday's employment report.
That comment sent stocks and bonds into a tailspin.

The trader said uncertainty ahead of Greenspan and the jobs report was evident in the Chicago Board Options Exchange's volatility index, which was up slightly in afternoon trading even as the market rose.
Typically the VIX moves in the opposite direction of the underlying market.
The VIX is calculated off prices of certain OEX options. The OEX was up 2.52 at 775.27 and the SPX was up 2.76 at 798.07.
The Dow industrial average .DJI was up 15 at 6,934.
The SPX trader added that if the jobs report is at all inflationary, the market could sell off sharply.
The OEX and SPX dealer said the jobs report -- and the market reaction to it -- could set the tone for a few months.
The only predominant activity was some call selling in select SPX contracts including the March 820s, 825s and 830s, the SPX trader said.
"I don't think it's because they think the market's going down, I just think the premium levels are so high in those calls that if we do rally, they're not going to go anywhere," he explained.

At the CBOE, the SPX March 820 call, with volume of about 2,470, was up 1/2 at 4-1/4. The March 825 call traded 1,685 contracts and gained 5/8 at 3-3/8. The March 830 call added 3/16 to 2-3/16. It traded about 2,665 contracts.
Overall, SPX put volume outpaced call volume at the CBOE by 24,181 to 13,667 at the CBOE by 1230 CST/1830 GMT.
The most active SPX option at the CBOE was the March 775 put, which traded about 3,345 contracts.
In the OEX, which typically has more volume than the SPX, calls outpaced puts by 28,514 to 24,795. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
